title: A visa is required almost everywhere
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: The Iranian passport gives visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to roughly 40 destinations and none of them are the countries people actually emigrate to. Every move starts from a standing refusal.

title: No US consular services inside Iran since 1980
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: The US embassy in Tehran has not issued visas since 1980, so every US visa application requires international travel to a third country before the process even begins.

title: US travel bans: restriction, lifting, reinstatement
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
era_note: Restricted 2017-2021; open 2021-2025; restricted again from June 2025; full suspension from 1 Jan 2026.
summary: Iran has been under some form of US entry restriction for most of the period since 2017. As of 1 January 2026 Iranian nationals face a complete suspension of both immigrant and non-immigrant visas.

title: Refusal rates far above average
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Where Iranians can apply, they are refused more often. Elevated refusal is priced into every plan: applications are made in duplicate, and refusal itself becomes evidence against the next application.

title: Administrative processing and 221(g) holds
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: A consular officer who cannot decide issues a 221(g) and puts the case into administrative processing. For Iranian applicants, especially in STEM, this is close to routine and has no deadline.

title: Canada screened Iranians by nationality, age and sex
category_name: Security screening, vetting and intelligence referral
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
era_note: Mandatory indicators abandoned August 2018; referral volumes stayed high.
summary: Before August 2018 Canada used a mandatory screening indicator for Iranian applications built on nationality combined with age and sex alone. Matching applicants were automatically referred to CBSA and CSIS. This is the single clearest documented instance of an Iranian man being screened for being an Iranian man.

title: Volume and duration of Canadian security screening
category_name: Security screening, vetting and intelligence referral
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Referral to security screening rarely produces a refusal. It produces years of silence. The harm is the delay, and the delay is the part nobody is accountable for.

title: US security advisory opinions and the Technology Alert List
category_name: Security screening, vetting and intelligence referral
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: The US equivalent: applicants whose field touches the Technology Alert List are referred for a Security Advisory Opinion. Iranian nationality plus a technical field is close to an automatic referral.

title: Conscription is compulsory, and it gates the passport
category_name: Military service and the male exit problem
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Every Iranian man aged 18-49 owes 18-24 months of military service, and a man who has not served or been exempted generally cannot get a passport. The exit door is locked from the inside before any destination country is involved.

title: Draft evasion as an asylum claim that is hard to win
category_name: Military service and the male exit problem
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Refusing conscription is a recognised basis for protection in principle, but proving it - and proving the punishment would be persecution rather than prosecution - is difficult and gendered.

title: Iran is outside the Apostille Convention
category_name: Documents, translation, legalisation and proof
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Iran is not a party to the 1961 Hague Convention, so no Iranian document can be apostilled. Every document needs the long consular legalisation chain instead.

title: Name transliteration inconsistency
category_name: Documents, translation, legalisation and proof
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Persian names have no single Latin spelling. Passport, degree, bank record and visa can each carry a different transliteration, and every mismatch reads to an officer as a possible identity discrepancy.

title: Police certificates that cannot be obtained
category_name: Documents, translation, legalisation and proof
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Most immigration programs require a police clearance from every country lived in. Obtaining an Iranian certificate generally requires presence in Iran or a legalised power of attorney, and the result may still be questioned.

title: Iranian credentials are slow and expensive to verify
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Credential evaluation is required for most skilled-migration and licensing routes. The Iranian chain has more steps than most, and verification depends on institutions that may not answer.

title: Sanctions and suspicion attach to Iranian universities
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Several Iranian universities carry export-control or sanctions designations. Graduates inherit the association, which affects admission, visa screening and employment even where the individual has no connection to the designated work.

title: Ranking and recognition penalties
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Strong Iranian universities are under-represented in global rankings for reasons partly unrelated to teaching quality - sanctions on indexing and collaboration, limited international co-authorship, and language. Graduates are then assessed against the ranking.

title: Bank accounts closed abroad for nationality
category_name: Banking, money movement and sanctions spillover
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Banks outside Iran have repeatedly closed or refused accounts for Iranian nationals who are lawfully resident and not covered by any sanction - over-compliance rather than legal requirement.

title: Money cannot move out of Iran through the banking system
category_name: Banking, money movement and sanctions spillover
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Iran is disconnected from SWIFT for most purposes. Family savings, property proceeds and salary history cannot be transferred by any traceable route - which is exactly the route immigration systems require.

title: Gold, crypto and stores of value
category_name: Banking, money movement and sanctions spillover
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Blocked from ordinary banking, Iranians turn to gold and cryptocurrency - and are then blocked from those too, or treated as suspicious for using them.

title: Export control closes whole industries
category_name: Work, licensing, export control and clearance
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Under the 'deemed export' rules, letting an Iranian national see controlled technical data counts as exporting to Iran. Because Iran is under arms embargo, the licence that would permit it is effectively unavailable - so defence, aerospace and parts of semiconductors simply do not hire.

title: Licensed professions require re-qualification
category_name: Work, licensing, export control and clearance
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Doctors, nurses, engineers, lawyers and teachers cannot practise on a foreign credential. Re-qualification costs years and money, and for Iranians the verification step that underpins it is the fragile one.

title: Name-based hiring discrimination
category_name: Work, licensing, export control and clearance
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Field experiments across several countries show identical CVs receive fewer callbacks under a Middle Eastern or Muslim-sounding name. The effect applies before any interview, so it is invisible to the person experiencing it.

title: Blaine, January 2020 - detained for ancestry
category_name: Borders, airports and secondary inspection
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Over a weekend in January 2020, US citizens and permanent residents of Iranian heritage were held for hours at the Peace Arch crossing and questioned about their politics and allegiance. Internal guidance later showed selection by nationality and birth year.

title: Routine secondary inspection and device searches
category_name: Borders, airports and secondary inspection
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Outside headline incidents, Iranian travellers report disproportionate secondary inspection, questioning about family and politics, and searches of phones and laptops at the border, where normal warrant protections are weakest.

title: Years of conditional status before anything is secure
category_name: Status, residency and citizenship timelines
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Between arrival and citizenship sit years of permits that must be renewed, each renewal a point at which the whole life can be refused.

title: Iran does not let citizenship go
category_name: Status, residency and citizenship timelines
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Iran does not recognise renunciation in practice and treats dual nationals as Iranian only. Naturalising elsewhere does not end the Iranian obligations - including, for men, military service.

title: Parents cannot visit
category_name: Family, reunification and visitors
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Visitor visas for Iranian parents are refused at high rates on 'ties' and 'intent' grounds. The practical effect is that grandparents never meet grandchildren and nobody attends anybody's funeral.

title: Locked out of the tools of the trade
category_name: Technology, platforms and digital exclusion
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: US platforms blocked Iranian users on sanctions grounds - including users who had left Iran years earlier - cutting off source control, cloud, payments and app distribution.

title: Everyday nationality friction
category_name: Discrimination and daily life
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Car hire, insurance, tenancy screening, payment processors and background-check vendors all run sanctions screens. Each one occasionally returns a false positive on an Iranian name or birthplace, and each must be argued individually.

title: The cost of indefinite uncertainty
category_name: Health, mental load and the cost of uncertainty
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Years of pending status with no decision date is a documented stressor distinct from a bad outcome. Waiting without a deadline is the specific harm.

title: Legal help is expensive and mostly unavailable
category_name: Asylum, legal process and representation
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Immigration law is complex, consequential and largely outside legal aid. Most people navigate it alone or pay heavily.

title: The one-way door
category_name: Return, exit and the one-way-door problem
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: For many Iranian men the decision to leave is effectively irreversible: conscription liability, political exposure or asylum claim all make return unsafe or impossible. Every other hurdle is faced with no fallback.

title: Selectee screening at US airports
category_name: Borders, airports and secondary inspection
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Beyond land borders, Iranian travellers report being marked SSSS on boarding passes far more often than chance would suggest. The mechanism is documented; the selection rates are secret.

title: The air route itself keeps disappearing
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Direct flights between Iran and Europe have repeatedly been suspended - by sanctions, by safety, by war and by single incidents. Each suspension strands people mid-journey and forces longer, costlier routings.

title: The English test itself became unavailable
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: In 2026 the standard English proficiency tests stopped being offered inside Iran - IELTS in January, then TOEFL, GRE and Duolingo after OFAC suspended the licence that permitted educational services to Iranians.

title: ATAS: refused with no reason given
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Iranian postgraduates in UK STEM subjects must obtain ATAS clearance. Iran is not on the exemption list, refusals are not explained, and a refusal blocks the visa entirely.

title: Sanctioned universities: the degree carries the designation
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Sharif University of Technology - Iran's leading engineering school - has been sanctioned by the EU, UK and Japan. Its graduates carry the association through every subsequent visa, job and clearance check.

title: IRGC conscription and Canadian inadmissibility
category_name: Military service and the male exit problem
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Canada listed the IRGC as a terrorist entity in June 2024. Men who were conscripted into IRGC-affiliated units - an assignment they did not choose - now face inadmissibility for 'membership' in a listed entity.

title: German asylum decisions on Iran got harsher as Iran got worse
category_name: Asylum, legal process and representation
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Germany's protection rate for substantively examined Iranian claims fell from 45% to 27% between 2023 and 2025, while repression inside Iran intensified. Men fare worse than women.

title: Getting money out legally, if you are a US person
category_name: Banking, money movement and sanctions spillover
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: OFAC permits sale and transfer of inherited property or property owned before becoming a US person. Everything else needs a specific licence, and the routing runs through third countries.

title: Iran charges you to leave, and limits what you take
category_name: Banking, money movement and sanctions spillover
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: A tiered departure tax rises with each trip in a solar year, and hard limits cap the currency, gold and goods that may leave with you.

title: Housing, licences and the ordinary machinery of settling
category_name: Discrimination and daily life
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: The unglamorous layer: finding a flat with no local credit history, exchanging a driving licence, enrolling children, and re-establishing every routine relationship that a settled person already has.

title: Nationality passes down, and so does the obligation
category_name: Family, reunification and visitors
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Iranian nationality descends from the father. A man who emigrates and has sons abroad passes them Iranian nationality - and with it, in principle, the conscription liability he left to escape.

title: Deported on arrival, holding a valid visa
category_name: Borders, airports and secondary inspection
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Between 2019 and 2021 Iranian students who had passed a year of vetting, been granted visas and flown to the United States were detained at the airport, had their visas revoked on the spot, and were put on a plane home.

title: Refused service by private businesses
category_name: Discrimination and daily life
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Shop staff, banks and platforms enforce sanctions themselves, at the counter, against customers who are lawfully present and often citizens. Speaking Persian in the wrong shop has been enough.

title: The appointment does not exist, and then it costs EUR 1,000
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Consular appointment systems are scraped by bots the instant slots open. The slots are free on the official site and unobtainable there; brokers resell them for hundreds of euros.

title: Iran's only consular presence in the US is a pass-through
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: There has been no Iranian embassy in the United States since 1980. The Interests Section, hosted inside the Pakistani embassy, is the only body authorised to provide Iranian consular services - and it decides almost nothing.

title: You must surrender your only passport to renew it
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Renewal requires submitting the existing Iranian passport. For six to fourteen weeks the applicant holds no Iranian travel document at all - and, if their status abroad depends on it, no way to prove anything.

title: The arrival catch-22
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: A bank account needs an address. A tenancy needs a bank account and a payslip. A job needs a bank account and a phone number. A phone contract needs an address and a credit check. Every door requires a key kept behind another door.

title: Moving a life, by weight
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Everything that is not paperwork has to physically travel, be stored, be sold or be abandoned. For Iranians the shipping route itself is constrained by sanctions and by export limits on the way out.

title: Everything must be done in person, in another city
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Biometrics, interviews, document collection and medical examinations each require physical attendance at a designated centre, often in another country, each on a date set by someone else.

title: Single points of failure in a paper chain
category_name: Logistics: appointments, queues, couriers and the physical mechanics
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: The legalised, translated, stamped original exists in one copy, and it travels by courier between countries that do not have reliable postal relations.

title: One person, many spellings
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Persian has no single Latin transliteration, so the same name is spelled differently on the passport, the degree, the bank record and the visa. Every mismatch reads to a system as a possible different person.

title: The spelling someone else chose, permanently
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: A clerk types the name wrong once, and the error propagates. Later systems are populated from the earlier record, so the original typo becomes the authoritative version and correcting it means correcting everything downstream.

title: The name as a flag
category_name: Names: transliteration, misspelling and identity mismatch
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Beyond mismatch, the name itself is a signal. It triggers sanctions screening false positives, changes callback rates on job applications, and marks the holder before any conversation happens.

title: Denied something you were entitled to, by mistake
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the agent who got it wrong
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Eligibility is decided at a counter by a person who may not know the rule. A wrong refusal is not recorded as a refusal - it is recorded as nothing - and the applicant simply does not have the thing they were entitled to.

title: The outcome depends on which officer you get
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the agent who got it wrong
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Discretionary standards - 'satisfied that', 'reasonable grounds', 'sufficient ties' - mean two identical files decided by two officers produce opposite results, and neither is wrong.

title: Nobody is accountable for the delay
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the agent who got it wrong
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Where a decision simply does not arrive, there is no decision to appeal, no service standard that binds, and no official who owns the file.

title: Single-entry visas, and only for the wrong subjects
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Multiple-entry US student visas were opened to Iranians in 2010 - but only for social sciences. Students in technical fields get single entry, so leaving the country once ends the visa. And nobody is told which category they are in.

title: Georgia: visa-free, and refused at the door
category_name: Borders, airports and secondary inspection
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Georgia is one of the few countries Iranians can enter without a visa, which made it a refuge. Since 2021 Iranians have been turned back at Tbilisi airport and the land borders in large numbers, with no reason given and no appeal.

title: The Netherlands barred Iranians from whole degree programmes
category_name: Education, credentials and academic recognition
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: From July 2008 Dutch policy forbade Iranian nationals - including Dutch citizens of Iranian descent holding no Iranian passport - from nine degree programmes and several research facilities. A court struck it down in 2010 as discrimination.

title: Australia: detained forever because Iran will not take you back
category_name: Asylum, legal process and representation
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Iran refuses to accept citizens deported against their will. Australia detains refused asylum seekers to facilitate removal. The result is detention with no end, lawful because the detainee could theoretically consent to return.

title: Turkey: the address decides, and the address is closed
category_name: Status, residency and citizenship timelines
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Turkey restricts residence permits by neighbourhood rather than by nationality. Iranians are named among the reasons for the policy, and an application at a closed address is rejected automatically.

title: UAE: residency cancelled while you were abroad
category_name: Status, residency and citizenship timelines
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: In 2026 Iranian residents of the UAE - including ten-year golden visa holders - found their residency revoked while they were outside the country, with no right of return and their property, accounts and children's schooling attached to the Emirates ID they no longer had.

title: Japan: the visa waiver that was cancelled underneath them
category_name: Visas, permits and the right to arrive
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Japan and Iran had mutual visa-free travel. Tens of thousands of young Iranian men came to work after the Iran-Iraq war; Japan cancelled the waiver in 1992 and the population collapsed. The clearest historical case of a door opening and shutting on one cohort.

title: The bail you cannot post because your family is in Iran
category_name: Discretion, clerical error and the agent who got it wrong
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Bond decisions turn on ties to the country - family, length of residence, employment. A recently-arrived student with all his relatives in Iran scores zero on every limb, so detention continues for having emigrated recently.

title: Being read as a threat, and starting to read yourself that way
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Twenty years of screening, secondary inspection and 'are you now or have you ever been' teaches a specific lesson: that you are a risk to be managed. People begin pre-managing themselves, and the self-editing costs more than the screening did.

title: The gratitude imperative
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Host societies expect appreciation, and the expectation is itself a form of control - it makes criticism, grief and ordinary complaint look like ingratitude. Scholars argue the duty does not actually exist.

title: Being counted as a cost
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Public opinion treats immigrants as a net drain on the welfare state, largely inaccurately. Living inside a story about yourself that the evidence does not support is its own chronic load.

title: The intimate market
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Dating and partner formation are stratified by ethnicity in measurable ways, and immigration status narrows the field further. The popular version of this claim is stronger than the data - which matters, because the belief does damage independent of the reality.

title: Vulnerability in relationships where status is asymmetric
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Where one partner's right to remain depends on the other, or on a job the other controls, ordinary relationship conflict acquires immigration consequences. The asymmetry is structural, not a matter of character.

title: The bandwidth tax
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Faced by any immigrant regardless of origin
summary: Scarcity of any kind consumes the mental capacity normally used for planning, problem-solving and self-control. This is measured, it is large, and it is the honest mechanism behind 'I used to have ideas'.

title: The body keeps the score
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: Chronic discrimination stress shows up physiologically - cardiovascular risk, metabolic and immune dysregulation. The pain and fatigue link is plausible and much less well evidenced than the cardiac one.

title: What it costs the career
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: The downstream effect of everything above: lower risk appetite, fewer moves, less negotiation, no venture. Not because of ability, but because the buffer that permits risk was spent on the process.

title: Depicted as something you are not
category_name: Psychological and social load, and what it costs downstream
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: Iranians are Persian, not Arab - Farsi is Indo-European, Arabic is Semitic - and Western media has spent forty years collapsing the distinction and casting Iranian men specifically as zealots and domestic tyrants. People arrive pre-characterised by films they have never seen.

title: The service card runs your life inside Iran, not just the exit
category_name: Military service and the male exit problem
applies_to_note: Requires both Iranian nationality and being male
summary: The military service completion or exemption card is a de facto internal identity document. Without one a man cannot get a passport, cannot get a driver's licence, cannot hold a government job and is 'not hired for high-paying jobs'. Emigration is blocked at the far end of a chain that already blocked everything else.

title: The law is on your side, and companies keep being fined for not knowing it
category_name: Work, licensing, export control and clearance
applies_to_note: Triggered by Iranian nationality, passport or place of birth
summary: DOJ has repeatedly penalised employers who used export control as a reason to hire only US citizens. ITAR's own definition of 'US person' includes permanent residents, asylees and refugees - so most of the exclusions Iranians meet are not merely unnecessary, they are unlawful.
